message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta.** Here’s how: | Step | What to do | Where / How | |------|------------|-------------| | **1** | Identify the source & details | Note the address, time(s) of disturbance, type of noise (construction, music, barking dogs, etc.), and any witnesses. | | **2** | Check the city’s noise ordinance | Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Chapter 10.1 of the Municipal Code) sets limits for residential and commercial areas. | | **3** | File the complaint | • **Online:** Use the 311 portal → “Noise Complaint” form.
• **Phone:** Call 404‑292‑2000 (the 311 hotline).
• **In person:** Visit the City Hall or the local police precinct. | | **4** | Follow up | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. The police or code enforcement will investigate; you can track status through the 311 portal or by calling the hotline. | ### Quick links * **311 portal (online filing):** * **Noise complaint form (PDF):** * **City’s noise ordinance text:** ### Tips * **Timing matters:** Most complaints are taken more seriously if reported during the day or early evening when the disturbance is ongoing. * **Document evidence:** Photos, videos, or audio recordings can help substantiate your claim. * **Know the hours:** Residential noise is generally prohibited after 10 p.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m. on weekends. Commercial noise rules differ by zone. * **Escalate if needed:** If the issue persists after initial investigation, you can request a follow‑up inspection or appeal the decision through the city’s administrative hearing process. Feel free to let me know if you’d like help drafting the complaint or locating the exact ordinance section relevant to your situation!
